title: Political Control Over Grant Allocation (OMB 2026)
bottleneck: A 2026 US proposal would give political appointees final say over federal research grants, reducing peer review to advisory status and allowing cancellation of awarded grants at any time. Physicians and researchers warn this replaces merit allocation with political compliance, injecting deep uncertainty into multi-year research planning. Multi-year grants already awarded face retroactive cancellation, which no peer-review reform can insure against.
why_it_blocks: Politicized funding destroys the stable, predictable support that long-horizon science requires and chills inquiry in disfavored areas. Long-term projects like longitudinal cohorts cannot survive retroactive cancellation risk.
current_state: As of mid-2026 the rule was proposed, not final; scientific societies mobilized opposition, with the outcome undecided. The episode illustrates how quickly institutional safeguards for science can be dismantled by executive action.
